chapters.accuracyNote: The composite is mostly faithful to the sources on the big confirmed facts (US location, six historical names, no cipher, item-histories-as-clues, the back-cover haiku, and the two attributed quotes), but it contains one clear factual error (smaller boxes have a dedicated CHAPTER, not a separate "book"), several details that conflate Lion's Share rules with confirmed-public-land/3-mile facts that do NOT appear in these front-matter pages, and it omits the book's explicit Part One vs. Part Two structure (four chapters in Part Two = the four smaller boxes).
chapters.visionSummary: Image-verified against ground-truth page scans (cropped with PIL for legibility). The composite (chapters/front-matter.md) contains one clear factual error: it says each of the four smaller boxes has "ONE dedicated book separate from The Lion's Share book," but page 10 plainly states the author "wrote four chapters... in Part Two of this book" — chapters, not books. The composite also drops the load-bearing scoping phrase "of the first twenty-three" from the page-16 sentence and omits the book's explicit Part One/Part Two structure (page 10 + page 16), which defines where Lion's Share vs. smaller-box clues live. The four "Treasure Location Confirmed" rules (public land, within 3 miles of a road, not buried/no digging, not dangerous) appear NOWHERE in the front matter (pages 1-17, verified by reading + keyword search of all front-matter sources); they originate in the Postscript/later author rules, so attributing them to the front matter is unsupported. Verbatim items check out: the six historical names (page 9, exact order), the back-cover haiku (cover.png), and the "millions of dollars / United States" headline. Pavese is attributed only as "—CESARE PAVESE" with no biographical detail (page 17); the "Italian poet (1908-1950)" descriptor is externally-added context. The actual Table of Contents (front-03-04) has NO "Part One/Part Two" labels — chapters are listed 1-23 sequentially, with the Final Poem at p.205 in the back matter — so the repo note labeling "Part Two = chapters 15-23 (nine chapters)" contradicts the book text, which says Part Two = four chapters.

I chose to create these four chapters as a way to avoid confusion as to what clues led to which box. You will find these chapters in Part Two of this book." The boxes each have a dedicated CHAPTER in Part Two of THIS book — NOT a separate book. The 'six figures' value is correct.

chapters.title: The 120 Carat Sapphire
chapters.accuracyNote: The composite is highly faithful: every checkable fact, number, place, and verbatim quote it includes is supported by the source transcriptions, with no contradictions found. Its main weaknesses are lost details (Bill Fernandez, National Semiconductor, the #1/#0 badges, the explicit in-treasure confirmation sentence, the IPO numbers, the Kimberly/parenting content, and the Tuyet Nguyet transition) and one analyst-added 'James Bond reference' interpretation that the book does not support (the book frames 007/'Scotty' as a Star Trek nod).
chapters.visionSummary: Chapter-01.md is image-verified accurate on all of its factual claims; the discrepancies are omissions of detail rather than inaccuracies. The page images (page-018-019.png, page-022-023.png) confirm: the p.19 sidebar "This 120-carat raw sapphire is a part of our treasure."; the p.23 confirmation "The sapphire pictured on the next page is the same as the one featured at the beginning of this chapter. Once owned by Mike Scott, it now is in our treasure."; Bowers Museum near Los Angeles; badge story (Woz #1, Jobs #0, "Scotty gave himself badge number 007."); 2,600 mineral specimens; origin Ratnapura/Sri Lanka; Eleanor Roosevelt and Mary Oliver epigraphs. Two real OMISSIONS exist: (1) the composite states the gist of in-treasure status but never quotes the two explicit treasure-confirmation statements; (2) the composite omits the Apple growth metrics on p.22 (doubled every three months for four years; Apple II + Apple III; first 5 1/2" floppy disk; over six million Apple II units; third-largest home-computer maker). NOTE: the book itself literally prints "5 1/2" floppy disk" — so the metadata transcription is faithful and the flag's "typo for 5 1/4-inch" theory is a book error, not a transcription error. The "James Bond reference" note is the composite's own analytical speculation (flagged as a question), not a book claim; the underlying badge fact (007) matches the image. Minor metadata transcription glitches found but not in the composite: metadata says "workstation badges" (image: "workplace badges") and "Scotty himself badge number 007" (image: "Scotty gave himself badge number 007").

chapters.title: The 100 Rings of Tuyet Nguyet
chapters.accuracyNote: The composite is substantively faithful on names, dates, item attributes, and major clue phrases, but it presents page-37 reported-speech advice as four standalone direct quotes (two clear misquotes) and drops the article 'a' in the 'golden bridge' quote; it also omits several concrete narrative and date details.
chapters.visionSummary: Image verification of chapter-02.md is largely consistent on facts but reveals a systematic quoting problem on the page-37 "Direct Instructions to Hunters." The book presents this guidance as conditional/reported speech attributed to Tuyet Nguyet ("She'd probably advise to not rush through these pages. She might encourage you to get to know these stories, to consider their content, and to not dismiss any details."), NOT as four standalone imperative quotes. The composite reformats them into quotation-marked imperatives, two of which ("Don't rush through these pages", "Don't dismiss any details") invert the book's "to not rush"/"to not dismiss" construction into fabricated "Don't..." imperatives — confirmed inaccuracies. The other two ("Get to know these stories", "Consider their content") match in substance but are misframed as standalone direct quotes. Separately, the Khmer imagery quote drops an article: the book reads "Golden lions guarded a golden bridge," not "guarded golden bridge." Spot-checks all verify against the images: the "hidden caches, secreted away within temple walls" phrase (page 35), "with metal and fire, forged each of our five treasure boxes" + "Over the course of eighteen months, Seth Gould..." (page 37), and "Angkor's land mass was the size of Los Angeles" (page 33) are all accurate. Core facts (dates, figures, provenance, LA comparison, Seth Gould) are reliable; the quotation fidelity on page 37 is the chapter's main weakness.

chapters.visionSummary: Image verification surfaced a systematic transcription defect in the page metadata that the composite partially inherited. The metadata mis-read the red-italic photo captions on BOTH p38 and p44/45 as "(just in our Treasure)" with in_treasure=true, when the actual page images clearly read "(not in our treasure)". The composite caught this for the Faberge egg (correctly listed NOT in treasure) but propagated the error for the Japanese puzzle box, wrongly listing it as a treasure item — it is in fact NOT in the treasure (the chapter's only actual treasure item is the gold & jade magnifying glass, plus the Lion's Share box itself). Separately, the composite's magnifying-glass date and value are wrong: the p42 sidebar reads "made around 1890 valued at over $23,000," not "~1900, valued $25,000+." All other load-bearing facts verify against the images: Bakersville is "about 6,000 nautical miles east of Japan and forty miles northeast of Asheville, NC" (p40, exact); the Lion's Share box has "seven actions required to open it," "yellow brass...sides, ...steel...top edge...textured iron...center locking panel," and "I left instructions with the box" (p42, exact); magnifying-glass material is "gold and jade by Michael Perkhin" (p43 body, confirming the metadata sidebar's "1-karat" is itself an error). Net: 2 confirmed inaccuracies (puzzle box treasure-status; magnifier date/value), 1 dismissed (egg claim correct; metadata was the wrong source).

chapters.visionSummary: Chapter 5 (pp.56-63) verified against ground-truth page images. The chapter's text quotes are largely accurate, with one notable exception. (1) The Art Smith design-philosophy quote is materially condensed/altered in the composite: the book (p.60) reads "A piece of jewelry is in a sense an object that is not complete . . . until you relate it to the body. Like line, form and color, the body is a material to work with. It is one of the basic inspirations in creating form." The composite renders it as "A piece of jewelry is...not complete until you relate it to the body." — dropping "in a sense an object that" and the final two sentences, presenting a paraphrase as a direct quote. Have faith.") all match the image (p.63), with the composite using fair shorthand for the phrase-table entries. (3) The date 1934 is genuinely on p.59 in the immediate context of Art proclaiming (as an eighth-grader) he would become a professional artist — the composite's pairing is accurate.
